title: Safe Deposit Boxes: Rent Notices, Paying Ahead and Ways to Pay Rent
content:
This quick reference covers the practical side of paying for Safe Deposit Boxes: the reminder a lessee receives, the lead time for any rent increase or decrease, paying several years at once, and the channels through which rent is accepted.

## Quick reference (identical for all six sizes, 3x5 through 10x20 Safe Deposit Box)

| Item | Setting |
|---|---|
| Rent notice sent ahead of each due date | 30 calendar days before |
| Minimum notice before a changed rent can take effect | 30 calendar days |
| Most rental years payable in advance | 3 |
| Reduction on each prepaid year beyond the current one | 5 percent of that year's net rent |
| Accepted payment channels | automatic payment from a PCB checking account; one-off transfer from a PCB checking account; cash; check |

## Rent notice

Before every rent due date the lessee is sent a notice of the rent coming due, 30 days ahead of that date.

## Changes to the rent

A new rent level never lands in the middle of a rental year. It can take effect only when the lease renews, and only at a renewal falling at least 30 days after the lessee was notified of the change. A renewal that comes sooner than that after the notice keeps the existing rent.

## Paying for more than one year

A lessee may pay up to 3 rental years in advance. Each prepaid year that lies beyond the current rental year is charged at its net rent reduced by 5 percent; the current year itself carries no prepayment reduction.

*Hypothetical illustration:* if a box's net rent for a year were 100.00, the current year would be paid at 100.00 and each later year paid ahead at 95.00.

## Accepted ways to pay

Rent may be paid by any one of the four channels in the table. With automatic payment, the named PCB checking account is debited on the rent due date.

**Who may be named for automatic payment.** The account designated for automatic rent payment must be a checking account that belongs to the same customer who holds the box and whose status is active. This is judged from the bank's own record of that particular checking account, its owner and its status, not from the customer's description of it. A checking account owned by someone else, or one that is not active, cannot be set up to pay the rent.

## Points of judgement

- *Can the lessee prepay four years?* No. The ceiling is 3 rental years.
- *Does the prepayment reduction touch the year currently being paid?* No. Only years after the current one receive it.
- *Can a rent change announced 20 days before a renewal apply at that renewal?* No. Fewer than 30 days separate the notice from that renewal, so the change waits for a later one.
